subject: Model fit evals & tool-calling schema tests — post-call recap and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>

Subject: Model fit evals & tool-calling schema tests — post-call recap and next steps

Alex — thanks again for the chat today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment.

Recap:
- Goal: Evaluate Redwood inference for BrightAI's content-enrichment pipeline (entity extraction + enrichment via third-party APIs) with strict JSON output and retries for transient failures.
- Main concerns you raised: JSON schema compliance, structured output retries, end-to-end latency for batched requests, and reproducible quality baselines for model/quantization choices.

Recommended starting evals (we offered during the call):
1) Model candidates to test (we'll run side-by-side):
   - redwood-13b-opt (fp16) — baseline for best quality across tool-calling tasks
   - redwood-7b-quant (8-bit, optimized kernels) — cost/latency tradeoff for high throughput
   - redwood-3b-quant (low-cost, good for high-volume tiers)
2) Tool/function-calling tests: JSON schema validation (strict/permissive modes), structured output retries with idempotency tokens, and end-to-end error modes (partial enrichment, third-party timeout).
3) Prompt/fixture set: I attached the initial prompt set we discussed (prompt_set_brightai_v1.jsonl) — please review; we can extend it with your edge cases.

Benchmarks and docs I referenced: linked here — https://docs.redwood.ai/benchmarks/2026-q2 and we put a short quick-bench PDF attached for your procurement/legal folks.

Proposed next steps:
- You: Share a representative sample of 200 payloads (anonymized) and the canonical JSON schema you want enforced. If there are different schemas per enrichment type, include them all.
- Us: We'll run a structured-output eval (schema compliance + correctness + retry-robustness) across the three model candidates, return a short report with p50/p95 latencies, schema-pass rates, and example failures. Estimated turnaround: 5 business days after we get samples.
- Schedule: Let's tentatively put a 30-min review on Wed 2026-06-17; I can send a calendar invite.

Attachments: prompt_set_brightai_v1.jsonl, redwood_quick_bench_q2.pdf

If that all looks good, reply with the sample payloads and the schema (or a link). Happy to run the eval next week.

Thanks,

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Model fit evals & tool-calling schema tests — technical follow-up

Alex — quick technical notes on retries, schema validation, and what we'll measure in the eval. Quoting Marissa's original recap below for context.

On retries/idempotency:
- Redwood's function-calling runtime supports idempotency tokens on a per-request basis. If you include an idempotency key in metadata, we propagate it through retries and ensure only one external enrichment webhook call is triggered for the same key (unless the downstream explicitly returns a non-idempotent response).
- Retry policy we plan to use for the eval: exponential backoff with max 3 retries for transient (5xx, network) errors. We will simulate third-party timeouts and verify that retries do not lead to duplicate side-effects when idempotency keys are present.

On JSON schema validation and structured output: 
- We support two validation modes in the eval: strict (reject any non-conforming output) and permissive (attempt to coerce/repair where possible and flag corrections). For production you can pick strict if you want guaranteed schema contracts; permissive can surface best-effort corrections for human-in-the-loop flows.
- We will run schema-first checks (schema validator v2), then a semantic check comparing expected entity values against ground truth where available. Schema-pass rate will be reported as a percentage per model/quantization.

Metrics we'll provide in the report:
- Schema pass rate (strict / permissive)
- Entity-level precision/recall (where labeled)
- p50/p95 latency (per-request and per-token) for cold vs warm KV-cache states
- Cost estimate per 1M requests across model candidates (rough)
- Example failures with suggested prompt fixes and fallback policies

Links and artifacts we'll drop in the shared Drive folder: structured_output_eval_plan.md (attached), evaluation scripts (repo link), and the benchmark PDF Marissa attached.

Two quick asks from us: 
1) Please confirm whether your enrichment webhook expects a single JSON array of entities or newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON) per call — that affects batching semantics.
2) If you have labeled ground truth for even a subset (50-100 items) that will let us report meaningful precision/recall numbers.

Happy to run the eval as soon as we have the payloads + schema. If you'd like, I can include a short runbook showing the difference between strict/permissive outputs and automated repair heuristics.

- Aditya
Aditya Rao
